section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch10 — Creativity & Thinking (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A typical multiple-choice or fill-in-the-blank exam question requires a student to narrow down all possible ideas to arrive at one single correct answer. According to Guilford, this type of thinking is called:
explanation: Convergent thinking narrows multiple pieces of information down to a single correct answer, in contrast to divergent thinking, which generates many original solutions.
